Remember the roles: the captain navigates and chooses the destination, the chief engineer keeps machinery running, and fishers bring in the catch. Each has a distinct duty aboard the same vessel.

This role does not suit people who suffer seasickness, fear water, cannot tolerate long absences from home, or need a stable schedule. Sea work has no fixed quitting time and carries strict safety demands.

A common path starts in a fishing family or coastal community, continues as a deckhand learning to cast and haul nets, and requires a fishing-vessel crew certificate. Workers can advance to captain or chief engineer, or move into more stable coastal aquaculture or vessel transport.
This role suits physically strong people who tolerate hardship, vessel motion, long periods offshore, and risk. It could fit you if you accept extended work away from land.

Fishing And Hunting Workers perform marine and freshwater harvesting, catch sorting and preservation, aquaculture harvesting, and related hunting management. They work on fishing vessels, at aquaculture sites, and on fishing docks. The occupation combines physical skill with traditional and modern fishery methods.

entries: Fishing And Hunting Workers harvest marine and freshwater species, sort and preserve catches, conduct aquaculture harvesting, and perform related hunting management. They work on fishing vessels, at aquaculture sites, and on fishing-port docks.
Choose fishing areas based on sea conditions and fish movements, then coordinate with the captain.
Operate casting, trawling, and hauling equipment to complete fishing operations.
Sort catches by species and size, then ice them for preservation.
Maintain nets, winches, and other fishing equipment and troubleshoot faults.
Harvest stock, feed animals, and maintain facilities at aquaculture sites.
Record catch volume and operating logs, then transfer catches for sale.

paragraphs: A typical voyage leaves port before dawn and travels for hours to the fishing grounds. The captain chooses a casting location using sea conditions and sonar. The crew deploys and tows the net together, then everyone hauls, sorts, ices, and boxes the catch. Rough seas send the vessel back to port. The trip ends after delivery to a fish market or buyer.

In one sentence, fishers bring fish out of the water, preserve the catch, and sell it. Work includes judging fish movements, operating nets, sorting and icing catches, maintaining equipment, keeping logs, and transferring catches.

AI will not replace Fishing And Hunting Workers, but it will change how they find fish. Fish-finding sonar, satellite sea forecasts, and AI catch analysis now supplement experience and charts. Casting, hauling, and sorting on deck still require people. Machines can show where fish are, but they cannot cast and retrieve the net.

paragraphs: A score of 3/10 indicates relatively low AI exposure because most work occurs at sea and on deck. AI assists fish detection and sea forecasts, but people still cast, haul, and sort the catch.

Relatively low exposure does not mean no change. AI makes fishing more precise and catch analysis more systematic. It reduces wasteful casting based on luck. Fishers who use sonar and forecasting tools and understand catch management work more efficiently and can earn more.

This career depends on vessel experience. Coastal fishery schools or maritime programs offer a starting point, and a crew certificate is mandatory. Focus on safety awareness and physical conditioning. Fishers who read sonar data and manage catches can earn more in the AI era, but consider the hardship and risk of life at sea.

Use fish detection and sea-forecast tools instead of relying only on instinct. Earn higher-level crew certificates and advance from deckhand toward captain or chief engineer for better income and safety protection.

Without experience, start in coastal aquaculture or as a vessel apprentice. Certification is key. Quantify voyage count, catch volume, and safety record on your resume. This work does not suit people who suffer severe seasickness or cannot tolerate hardship.

Do not hire on strength alone. Assess safety awareness and ability to learn technology. Crews need people who use sonar and forecasting tools, handle catches well, and tolerate life at sea. Profit sharing and stronger protections can improve retention.

paragraphs: The largest career risk is not AI but the sea. Waves and fatigue directly threaten fishers, making safety awareness and respect more important than anything else.

The largest career risk is not AI but the unpredictability of the sea. Waves, machinery failures, and long periods offshore make maritime work far more dangerous and demanding than land-based jobs. Fishing also carries high occupational injury risk.
